title: Does faithful IIT 4.0 big-Phi track Kolmogorov (LZ) complexity? — Phi || LZ vs Phi perp Shannon-entropy (H_287) dual-measure contrast
question: Across an ECA panel, does faithful state-averaged big-Phi co-vary with normalised LZ76 complexity (Pearson r >= 0.5), i.e. does Phi track ALGORITHMIC complexity (unlike Shannon entropy in H_287)?
engine: HEXAD/IIT4/lib (reused, NOT reinvented): iit4_eca.eca_tpm + iit4_bigphi.big_phi + iit4_bit/iit4_pow2 (via stdlib/consciousness/*). LZ76 (Kaspar-Schuster) + Pearson/Spearman = generic stats inlined in the per-experiment harness; eca_next_row reuses iit4_bit.
runtime: $0 mac-local · hexa-only · LLM none · NO GPU · deterministic (cross-process byte-identical)
toolchain_note: built via fix-1180 bypass: HEXA_MAC_BUILD_OK=1 HEXA_LANG=<root> hexa.real.bak-2026-05-22-pre-no-hxc build <src> -o <bin> (PATH hexa regressed to bare hexa-cc; old-driver build calls self/native/hexa_v2 transpiler directly). See reference-life-cycle-hexa-run-gotchas.

metric_defs.LZ_norm: Lempel-Ziv 1976 (Kaspar-Schuster) complexity of the spacetime diagram — NL=14 ring evolved T=64 steps from a single centre seed, row-major NL*T bit string, distinct-phrase parse, normalised c*log2(L)/L (random string -> ~1).
metric_defs.Phi_mean: mean over all 2^n states of big_phi(tpm, n, st)[0] (n=4 exact).

seed_hypothesis_H1: Pearson r(LZ_norm, Phi_mean) >= 0.5 (Phi tracks algorithmic complexity).

rule_90.note: WITNESS: non-trivial LZ (Sierpinski self-similar) yet Phi=0 — LZ over-predicts

contrast_with_H287.meaning: Phi aligns with ALGORITHMIC complexity (how incompressible the spacetime pattern is), NOT statistical information (how many bits / Shannon entropy). Same 10-rule panel, orthogonal findings.

finding: Faithful causal IIT 4.0 big-Phi strongly tracks Kolmogorov (LZ) complexity (Pearson r=0.831, Spearman rho=0.936 over a 10-rule panel): constants/identity (low-LZ, Phi=0) rise monotonically to integration/chaos rules (high-LZ, high-Phi). THE KEY FINDING IS THE CONTRAST WITH H_287: on the identical panel, Shannon entropy was orthogonal to Phi (r=0.363) while Kolmogorov complexity aligns (r=0.831) — Phi is the same axis as ALGORITHMIC complexity (how incompressible the spacetime pattern is), NOT statistical information (how many bits). Honest caveat: rule 90 (Sierpinski self-similar, LZ=0.24 non-trivial) has Phi=0 — LZ over-predicts integration for self-similar patterns, so LZ is a strong correlate but NOT sufficient. Binary direction (low<->high) trusted, mid-range magnitude hedged.
honest_limits: L1: n=4 small, 10-rule panel — direction robust, exact r panel-dependent.
L2: LZ76 is ONE algorithmic-complexity estimator (block-entropy/CTW/other seeds differ); endpoints (constant=low, chaos=high) definition-robust, mid magnitude dependent.

L3: rule 90 over-prediction (KEY caveat) — Sierpinski fractal has non-trivial LZ but Phi=0 (sync-death); LZ is a strong correlate but NOT sufficient for integration. Finding is a TREND not an identity.
L4: Phi_mean averages a state-dependent quantity (FAITHFUL_REMEASURE 4) — direction robust, magnitude hedge.
L5: ECA rules are complexity/integration proxies, not the things themselves; labels are substrate-themes, not phenomenal claims.
L6: structure-cut big-Phi, not full-IIT4 absolute calibration; correlation conclusion robust to scale offset.
L7: verdict is a measurement fact on a toy substrate, NOT the metaphysical claim 'consciousness = algorithmic complexity'.

verify_fence.claim: H_288 faithful IIT 4.0 big-Phi TRACKS Kolmogorov (LZ76) complexity across a 10-rule ECA panel (Pearson r=0.831, Spearman rho=0.936), in CONTRAST to Shannon entropy which is orthogonal (H_287 r=0.363) — Phi aligns with algorithmic complexity not statistical information; rule 90 (Sierpinski, LZ=0.24, Phi=0) is an honest over-prediction witness; deterministic toy-substrate outcome, NOT an atlas identity
